```sql
-- name: top_products
-- owner: merchandising
-- params: tenant_id, from, to, limit
WITH lines AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT pv.product_id,
         ol.order_id,
         pv.id AS variant_id,
         ol.quantity,
         ol.line_total_cents
    FROM order_lines ol
    JOIN orders o           ON o.id = ol.order_id
    JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = ol.variant_id::uuid
   WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
     AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
     AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
     AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
),
agg AS (
  SELECT product_id,
         sum(quantity)         AS quantity,
         sum(line_total_cents) AS revenue_cents
    FROM lines
   GROUP BY product_id
),
oc AS (
  SELECT product_id, count(*) AS order_count
    FROM (SELECT DISTINCT product_id, order_id FROM lines) d
   GROUP BY product_id
),
vc AS (
  SELECT product_id, count(*) AS variant_count
    FROM (SELECT DISTINCT product_id, variant_id FROM lines) d
   GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       oc.order_count,
       agg.quantity,
       agg.revenue_cents,
       vc.variant_count
  FROM agg
  JOIN oc       ON oc.product_id = agg.product_id
  JOIN vc       ON vc.product_id = agg.product_id
  JOIN products p ON p.id = agg.product_id
 ORDER BY agg.quantity DESC, agg.revenue_cents DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De kostenpost in het origineel is de externe sort van ~81.000 regels op `(p.id, o.id)`, nodig voor `count(DISTINCT o.id)` en `count(DISTINCT pv.id)`. Deze herschrijving berekent de distincts via kleine `DISTINCT`-subsets per product, waardoor die grote sort verdwijnt. Het resultaat, de kolomtypen en de ORDER BY blijven gelijk, maar de werkelijke versnelling moet je met EXPLAIN ANALYZE op de productiedata verifiëren.
